notes: Both coders found the same two documents (AI Use Policy Rev FY26, Teach with AI page) and both set stance to delegates with the same three tiers. Main disagreements: (1) unit_stance for disclosure and attribution duties (A permit, B neutral), resolved as neutral because those sentences take no position on whether AI may be used; (2) policy_type for tier definitions (P05 vs P01/P02 for the no-use and extensive-use tier lines), resolved as P05 because they define a tier and are not a default rule; (3) actor/phase for quoted sample-syllabus text and faculty-facing rationale, resolved by who the sentence addresses; (4) modality for suggested assignment ideas (must/may/informs/should), resolved as should for all because the page recommends them; (5) single type splits: P56 vs P61 for scope (P61), P50 vs UNCOVERED for breach reporting (P50), P63 vs UNCOVERED for the community training duty (UNCOVERED), P44 vs P09 for 'explain why you are asking them to use it' (P09), P14 vs P12 for study-partner quizzing (P14), P48 vs P47 for the site's AI-assistance note (P48), P18 vs P61 for spell-check allowed under No Use (P18), P56 vs P36 for 'does not replace other integrity policies' (P56). Matching used source position; adjacent anchors that covered different sentences (tier description vs example uses, fake-citation paper vs AI-generated-code idea, 'ethical considerations' vs 'do not replace human judgment') were treated as separate units, not matches. A merged 'brainstorm but cannot write the paper' into one unit; it was split into two (B's units), so the permission clause counts as matched and the prohibition clause as only_B. All 30 one-coder units were real statements and were kept; none were dropped. Final file has 107 units (53 and 54). UNCOVERED: advising non-substitute, human review of automated administrative decisions, no sole reliance on AI outputs for decisions about individuals, community training duty, judgment-based evaluation of suspected misuse. new_types empty on both sides.
